objective: Implement the Agent Runtime-owned fail-closed sequential execution controller on top of Issue #58: preflight an entire typed TaskGraph through the injected PolicyValidator, revalidate every SemanticAction immediately before dispatch through an injected typed adapter, record deterministic execution states, and stop later dispatch after terminal outcomes without modifying shared contracts, Motion, World Model, firmware, integration fixtures, or safety configuration.
decision_supported: Can Agent Runtime deterministically and fail-closed orchestrate already-typed semantic actions through an injected adapter while preserving policy, execution, Motion, and World Model ownership boundaries?
acceptance: ExecutionController accepts a typed TaskGraph plus explicitly injected PolicyValidator and typed ActionAdapter. A non-TaskGraph input, duplicate step_id or action_id, missing, self, forward, or cyclic dependency, or a non-allow full-graph policy report produces a typed fail-closed execution report before the first adapter call. Tests: test_policy_rejection_prevents_first_dispatch and test_graph_structure_errors_prevent_first_dispatch.

For a valid graph whose adapter returns contract-valid completed ActionResults, the controller dispatches actions strictly in graph step order and records deterministic pending, dispatched, and succeeded transitions for each step. Test: test_valid_graph_dispatches_strictly_in_order_and_records_transitions.

Immediately before each adapter call, the controller rechecks that step through the same injected PolicyValidator and the same exact-action confirmation collection used for preflight. A later action mutated after preflight is denied before reaching the adapter. Test: test_action_is_revalidated_immediately_before_dispatch.

Existing ActionResult outcomes map deterministically to controller states: completed to succeeded, failed to failed, timeout to timed_out, canceled to cancelled, and safe_stop to stopped. Any failed, timed_out, cancelled, or stopped step prevents all later ordinary actions from being dispatched. Test: test_terminal_action_result_stops_later_steps.

TimeoutError becomes a typed timed_out controller record; any other adapter exception becomes a typed failed controller record. A non-ActionResult return or an ActionResult whose action_id differs from the dispatched action fails closed and prevents later dispatch. Tests: test_adapter_exceptions_become_typed_terminal_records and test_invalid_adapter_result_fails_closed.

At each controller dispatch boundary, a contract-valid STOP SemanticAction takes priority over every not-yet-dispatched ordinary action, uses the existing ToolRegistry and PolicyValidator rules, is dispatched at most once, and prevents every remaining pending ordinary action from being dispatched. Repeating the same STOP action_id is idempotent. Cancellation of an already-active Motion goal remains Issue #52. Test: test_stop_request_preempts_remaining_steps_and_is_idempotent.

Repeated delivery of the same action_id to the same running controller cannot cause another adapter call after that action_id has been dispatched. The duplicate result is deterministic. Restart-persistent and cross-process deduplication remain Issue #64. Test: test_duplicate_execute_request_never_redispatches_action_ids.

The controller never mutates the supplied TaskGraph, TaskStep, SemanticAction, parameters, PolicyReport, or ActionResult. Model dumps before and after execution remain equal. Test: test_controller_does_not_mutate_task_graph_or_actions.

Controller output is execution-orchestration evidence only. It does not write WorldState or WorldEvent, create VerificationResult, set verified_complete, claim task completion, or claim Motion, MCU, simulation, or physical execution beyond the injected fake adapter result. Test: test_controller_report_is_orchestration_only.

The package exposes only the minimum controller types required by Agent Runtime consumers, all focused and repository-required checks pass, and the Git-visible diff relative to fixed stacked base ed3aa21233040ef19239206d18721f13eb23d621 contains only the four allowed paths. Test: test_execution_controller_public_exports_are_available.
commands: python3 -m pytest tests/unit -k "execution_controller or policy_validator or tool_registry" -v
evidence: Pre-implementation baseline output showing 129 existing Agent Runtime, PolicyValidator, ToolRegistry, and observe-plan-act tests pass while no execution_controller module, controller Task Packet, controller test, implementation PR, or controller branch exists.

Focused red-test output showing the new execution-controller tests fail before implementation because the controller, typed adapter port, transition records, dispatch-time revalidation, STOP preemption, and duplicate suppression do not exist.
Focused green-test output for every normal, boundary, and failure behavior named in acceptance.
Fake-adapter call history proving strict action order and zero calls for malformed graphs, policy denial, confirmation_required, invalid adapter results, and all steps after a terminal result.
Policy spy and mutated-second-step regression proving one full-graph preflight plus immediate per-step revalidation through the same Issue #58 PolicyValidator.
Deterministic transition evidence covering pending, dispatched, succeeded, failed, timed_out, cancelled, and stopped.
STOP call history proving STOP is dispatched once before remaining pending ordinary actions and an identical repeated STOP request does not redispatch.
Duplicate-request call-count evidence proving a previously dispatched action_id is not dispatched twice within the same running controller.
Before-and-after TaskGraph, SemanticAction, parameters, PolicyReport, and ActionResult dumps proving controller input immutability.

Type and attribute assertions proving the execution report is not VerificationResult, contains no WorldState write or verified_complete flag, and makes no Motion, MCU, simulation, physical-execution, or task-completion claim.
Full make test, contract, scenario, context, demo-scripted, and make check output.

Task Packet validation and Git boundary output proving the final diff contains only execution_controller.py, its unit test, the minimal package export, and this Task Packet relative to ed3aa21233040ef19239206d18721f13eb23d621.
stop_conditions: Issue #58 commit ed3aa21233040ef19239206d18721f13eb23d621 is rejected, changed, unavailable to the implementation owner, or no longer approved as the stacked boundary.
Implementation requires changing PolicyValidator, ToolRegistry, tool_schemas, planner, local_model, another Agent Runtime module beyond the minimal package export, or any path outside allowed_paths.
Implementation requires adding a second action, parameter, confirmation, or policy allow-list instead of consuming the Issue #58 PolicyValidator.
Implementing invalid-graph rejection requires changing TaskGraph, SemanticAction, ActionResult, ActionStatus, DispatchState, DeviceState, or any interfaces or libs/contracts definition.

STOP is required to interrupt an already-blocking adapter call, cancel an active Motion goal, introduce concurrency, threading, asynchronous scheduling, or define a cross-module cancellation contract.
A real Motion adapter, robot/control write, firmware behavior, MCU transport, hardware behavior, or safety-configuration change becomes necessary.
Duplicate suppression is required to survive process restart or coordinate across processes, or requires an append-only correlation ledger; that belongs to Issue #64.
The controller must fabricate, persist, or rewrite ActionResult, generate clock or identifier evidence, write WorldEvent or WorldState, emit VerificationResult, or claim task completion.

Implementation requires modifying tests/integration, demo_scripted, deployment, CI, Backend, Perception, World Model, simulation, hardware, or another module without separate Owner approval and a revised Task Packet.

The fixed stacked base changes, the worktree contains overlapping user modifications, Owner delegation is withdrawn or disputed, or a required command fails for a reason that cannot be fixed within allowed_paths.
risks_and_fallbacks: Idempotency is limited to the same running ExecutionController. If restart-persistent or cross-process exactly-once behavior is required, stop and defer to Issue #64.
STOP preempts not-yet-dispatched actions at a deterministic controller boundary. If active-call interruption is required, stop and coordinate with Issue #52 and the Motion Owner.
Fake-adapter success proves controller sequencing and error handling only. It is not Motion, MCU, simulation, physical-execution, or completion evidence.
No controller-owned wall-clock timeout is added. Timeout state is derived only from a typed adapter result or TimeoutError; a runtime deadline scheduler requires a separately approved design.
